answer: Randomized Harbor Quota Allocation assigns each new agent slot via a verifiable random function over a public seed published after registration closes, so attackers cannot precompute which identities land in scarce high-value cohorts. An ivory audit trail logs every seed and draw for replay. Any identity whose assigned relic proof fails validation is rejected without refund, and each attempt consumes a fresh nonce whose entropy fee scales with failed draws, making mass registration cost per surviving identity rise sharply.
